method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Opportunistic education on oral hygiene and dental access** can prevent caries and odontogenic infection.
claims.source_text: Opportunistic education for families on good oral hygiene practices and how to access dental services can prevent dental caries and odontogenic infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Caries affects more than 40% of Australian children** and can start as soon as teeth erupt. Early childhood caries mainly affects the upper front teeth, in breast- and bottle-fed children who keep feeding or comfort-sucking at night.
claims.source_text: Dental caries occurs in more than 40% of Australian children and can begin as soon as teeth erupt during infancy … Early childhood caries mainly affects the upper front teeth, and is seen in both breast and bottle-fed children who continue to feed/comfort suckle at night
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wipe infants' teeth and gums; from over 12 months, brush twice daily with a smear of paediatric fluoridated toothpaste**, done or supervised by a parent. **Annual dental review.**
claims.source_text: Infants can have their teeth and gums wiped with a clean cloth or baby toothbrush. Children >12 months old should have twice daily brushing with a smear of paediatric fluoridated toothpaste, performed or supervised by parents until competent … Annual dental review is recommended
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Persistent thumb-sucking or dummy use after 3 years: dental consultation and cessation counselling.**
claims.source_text: Dental consultation and cessation counselling is recommended for children with persisting habits after 3 years of age
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about** cardiac conditions that may need endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures, and medicines that reduce saliva (e.g. antihistamines, anticonvulsants, antidepressants) or cause gum hypertrophy (e.g. phenytoin).
claims.source_text: Cardiac conditions which may indicate need for infective endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures … Medications which impact saliva production (eg antihistamines, anticonvulsants, antidepressants) or cause gum hypertrophy (eg phenytoin)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **'Lift the lip'** to examine the upper front teeth and gums; look for white or brown spots or lines at the gum line that don't brush off.
claims.source_text: 'Lift the lip' to ensure thorough examination of upper front teeth and gums … Look for early signs of decay including white or brown spots/lines along the top of the tooth adjacent to the gum line which don't brush off
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Abscess signs:** tender gingival swelling or erythema, a draining gingival sinus, facial cellulitis over the tooth, submandibular or periorbital areas, trismus. **Fever and systemic symptoms may be absent.**
claims.source_text: Abscess may be indicated by tender gingival swelling or erythema draining sinus from the gingiva erythema and cellulitis of facial skin overlying tooth, submandibular or periorbital areas trismus fever and systemic symptoms may be absent
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once an abscess has formed, extraction or root canal therapy is usually required.** Definitive treatment, i.e. extraction, is still needed after pain and infection are treated.
claims.source_text: Once a dental abscess or infection has formed, extraction or root canal therapy is usually required to remove the source of the infection … Definitive treatment of the carious tooth ie extraction will still be required after treatment of pain and infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give antibiotics for spreading infection, systemic signs, or when definitive dental treatment will be delayed more than 24 hours.**
claims.source_text: Antibiotics should be prescribed in cases of spreading infection and/or systemic signs of infection, or where definitive dental treatment is likely to be delayed >24 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Localised infection:** e.g. **amoxicillin 25 mg/kg (max 500 mg) orally tds.**
claims.source_text: Localised infection: eg amoxicillin 25 mg/kg (max 500 mg) orally TDS
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Spreading, no systemic features:** e.g. **amoxicillin/clavulanate 22.5/3.2 mg/kg (max 875/125 mg) orally bd for 5 days.**
claims.source_text: Spreading infection without systemic features: eg amoxicillin/clavulanate 22.5/3.2mg/kg (max 875mg/125mg) orally BD for 5 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Spreading infection with severe or systemic features:** e.g. **IV amoxicillin/clavulanate 6-hourly.** The page's dose figure is ambiguous and is not restated here — see Unresolved.
claims.source_text: Spreading infection with severe or systemic features: eg. amoxicillin/clavulanate 25/5 mg (max 1/0.2 g) IV 6 hourly
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow local susceptibility patterns.**
claims.source_text: Antimicrobial recommendations may vary according to local antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, please refer to local guidelines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bleeding after treatment** comes from a disturbed clot or a bleeding disorder. **Assess haemodynamic status**, rinse the mouth with cold water, and **bite on gauze for 30 minutes**; if bleeding continues, consider tranexamic-acid-soaked gauze. Treat any bleeding disorder; surgical dressing or sutures may be needed.
claims.source_text: Dental socket bleeding Can occur after treatment if child disturbs blood clot or due to a bleeding disorder … Assess and manage haemodynamic status Clean mouth with cold water Provide local pressure with gauze (bite down if able for 30 minutes) If ongoing bleeding, consider gauze soaked in tranexamic acid Treat bleeding disorder if applicable May need surgical dressing and suturing
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe bleeding:** IV access, FBE, coagulation studies, cross-match, IV fluids, firm pressure; **discuss with maxillofacial surgery and haematology.**
claims.source_text: Severe bleeding: IV access, FBE, coags, cross match, IV fluids, firm pressure, discuss with maxillofacial surgery and haematology
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usually no intervention.** Extract if very loose, an inhalation risk, interfering with breastfeeding, or ulcerating the tongue, frenulum or lip.
claims.source_text: Natal teeth Usually do not require intervention Indications for extraction: very loose, inhalation risk, difficulties breastfeeding or traumatic ulcerations of the tongue/frenulum/lip
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the specialist paediatric dental team** for an abscess with severe or systemic features needing admission, or a child whose medical, developmental or behavioural needs call for specialist dental, anaesthetic or haematology input.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with specialist paediatric dental team when Dental abscess with severe or systemic features requiring admission Children with underlying medical, developmental or behavioural issues likely to benefit from specialist dental, anaesthetic or haematology input
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** if specialist dental or maxillofacial care is not available locally.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Specialist dental or maxillofacial assessment and management is required and is not locally available
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** suitable for oral therapy, with cellulitis improving and extraction planned or done.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Suitable for oral therapy Cellulitis improving and extraction planned or complete
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Public dental access** is set by each state; some children qualify for the Child Dental Benefits Schedule.
claims.source_text: Each state has eligibility criteria for access to public dental services … Some children will also be eligible for the Child Dental Benefits Schedule which subsidises dental treatment through public or private dental services
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Dental conditions - non traumatic' (Last updated June 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Dental_conditions_non_traumatic/, retrieved 2026-09-23
